root_cause.text: In hv_netvsc's netvsc_copy_to_send_buf(), skb fragment page-buffer entries were incorrectly treated as always directly kernel-mapped by converting their PFNs with phys_to_virt(), even though they can reference highmem pages outside the direct map.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that the function "copies page buffer entries into the VMBus send buffer using phys_to_virt() on the entry PFN" and that skb fragments "reference page cache or user pages, which on 32-bit x86 with CONFIG_HIGHMEM=y can live above the LOWMEM boundary," causing phys_to_virt() to yield an invalid direct-map address and memcpy() to fault; the patch replaces this with per-page kmap_local_page() mapping.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In hv_netvsc's netvsc_copy_to_send_buf(), skb fragment page-buffer entries were incorrectly treated as always directly kernel-mapped by converting their PFNs with phys_to_virt(), even though they can reference highmem pages outside the direct map.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit states that the function "copies page buffer entries into the VMBus send buffer using phys_to_virt() on the entry PFN" and that skb fragments "reference page cache or user pages, which on 32-bit x86 with CONFIG_HIGHMEM=y can live above the LOWMEM boundary," causing phys_to_virt() to yield an invalid direct-map address and memcpy() to fault; the patch replaces this with per-page kmap_local_page() mapping.

intent_record.intent_summary: Include `linux/highmem.h` so the file has the required highmem declarations for correct compilation and use of high-memory helpers.
intent_record.what: A single header include was added: `#include <linux/highmem.h>` after the existing `#include <linux/mm.h>` line.
intent_record.how: This makes high memory APIs, macros, and declarations from `linux/highmem.h` available to the compilation unit, enabling use of highmem-related functionality or fixing build issues caused by missing declarations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix packet-buffer copying to safely map and copy physical memory page-by-page across page boundaries instead of using a single direct virtual address.
intent_record.what: The code replaces direct virtual-address copying from each packet buffer entry using `phys_to_virt(pb[i].pfn << HV_HYP_PAGE_SHIFT)` plus a separate offset with a new loop that computes a physical address including the offset, converts it page-by-page via `phys_to_page()`, maps each page temporarily with `kmap_local_page()`, copies a bounded chunk using `offset_in_page()` and `PAGE_SIZE`, then unmaps with `kunmap_local()` until the full length is copied.
intent_record.how: At runtime, copying now safely handles source data that may start at an offset and span across multiple physical pages instead of assuming a single directly addressable contiguous virtual mapping. This prevents incorrect memory access when a buffer crosses page boundaries or resides in memory that should be accessed through temporary page mapping.

grouping_result.intent: Fix packet-buffer copying to safely map and copy physical memory page-by-page across page boundaries instead of using a single direct virtual address.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix packet-buffer copying to correctly handle physical memory that may span page boundaries by using proper high-memory page mapping support.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the root cause by replacing incorrect assumptions about direct kernel mapping with proper high-memory page mapping and page-by-page copying across boundaries, which is exactly the issue with skb fragment pages residing in highmem.

candidates.rationale: This directly embodies the root cause: converting a PFN from an skb fragment page-buffer entry into a kernel virtual address with phys_to_virt(), incorrectly assuming the page is always in the direct map. Highmem pages may not be directly kernel-mapped, making this unsafe and invalid.

This dereferences and copies from the virtual address obtained via the unsafe phys_to_virt() conversion. It is the operation that triggers the vulnerability when src refers to a highmem page or spans beyond a safely mapped range.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is the root cause: it converts the PFN from a page-buffer entry into a kernel virtual address with phys_to_virt(), incorrectly assuming the referenced page is always directly mapped. skb fragment pages can be highmem and not safely accessible through the direct map.

This statement consumes the invalid direct-map virtual address derived from the PFN and performs the actual read. When src refers to a highmem or otherwise non-direct-mapped page, this copy dereferences unsafe memory and manifests the vulnerability.

The only change in this commit is shifting by `HV_HYP_PAGE_SHIFT` instead of `PAGE_SHIFT`, which addresses Hyper-V page size semantics, not the highmem/direct-map safety issue.
